rounds.text: N G Industries Ltd trades at a compelling discount, with a price-to-book ratio of just 1.05x [E2] and an EV/EBITDA of 11.71x compared to the sector benchmark of 16.58x [E11]. A discounted cash flow model values the intrinsic worth at Rs 236 per share against a current market price of Rs 105 [E42], providing a substantial margin of safety of 55.4% [E43]. The company operates on an exceptionally secure financial footing as it is almost debt free [E48], carrying a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.05x [E37] alongside positive free cash flow of Rs 0.87 Cr [E36] and a solid dividend yield of 3.33% [E4. Fundamental momentum is showing strong recent acceleration, highlighted by a 105% year-on-year surge in net profit [E57], expanding operating margins [E59], and quarterly operating margins rising to 10% in June 2026 from 9% in the prior-year quarter [E31]. Conceded: 10-year compounded sales growth is stagnant at 0% [E14] and return on equity remains low at 4.2% [E13].

The fundamental operating performance of N G Industries Ltd reveals a multi-year growth stall, evidenced by a 10-year compounded sales growth rate of 0% and a 3-year contraction of -4% [E14, E16]. Profitability metrics are structurally depressed, underscored by a trailing twelve-month profit growth collapse of -74% [E21] and a meager 3-year median return on equity of just 2% [E28]. Furthermore, operating margins exhibit a clear structural deterioration, carrying a decreasing trend over the last four years alongside poor cash conversion where operating cash flow sits at just 0.55x of reported profit for March 2026, signaling potential issues with receivables or accruals [E32, E34]. Quality of earnings is further compromised by the inclusion of Rs 1.13 Cr in other income [E54], masking weaker core operational results while the stock sits depressed at only 8% of its 52-week range [E5]. Conceded: the company maintains a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.05x with a healthy dividend yield of 3.33% [E4, E37].

Conceded: 10-year compounded sales growth is 0% [E14], 3-year sales growth is -4% [E16], and TTM profit growth dropped -74% [E21]. However, the bear ignores that 5-year compounded profit growth stands at a robust 19% [E19], and recent operational momentum shows quarterly sales up 14% and net profit surging 105% year-over-year [E56, E57]. While the bear highlights decreasing margins and low median ROE [E28, E32], quarterly operating margins actually expanded by one percentage point year-over-year in June 2026 [E31], and the company maintains solid positive free cash flow of Rs 0.87 Cr alongside an exceptionally conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.05x [E36, E37]. Conceded: operating cash flow sits at 0.55x of reported profit for March 2026 [E34], but this must be weighed against the company's continuous ability to generate actual positive operating cash flow of Rs 0.96 Cr and reward shareholders with a healthy 3.33% dividend yield [E35, E50]. Finally, the stock trading at just 8% of its 52-week range [E5] combined with a price-to-book of 1.05x [E2] represents deep mispricing relative to intrinsic value models that do not rely purely on stale multi-year averages [E42].

Conceded: 5-year compounded profit growth stands at 19% [E19] and the company generates positive free cash flow of Rs 0.87 Cr alongside a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.05x [E36, E37]. However, the bull's reliance on recent quarterly profit surges ignores the severe trailing collapse where TTM profit growth plummeted by -74% [E21] and 3-year sales growth contracted by -4% [E16]. The bull points to a June 2026 margin expansion [E31], yet the structural multi-year trend shows operating margins have been decreasing over the last 4 years [E32]. Conceded: the company paid dividends and maintained positive operating cash flow [E35, E50], but cash conversion sits at a weak 0.55x of reported profit for March 2026, meaning profits are far ahead of cash and point to receivables or accruals issues [E34]. Furthermore, the low stock price sitting at just 8% of its 52-week range [E5] reflects persistent long-term stagnation, including a 10-year compounded sales growth of 0% [E14] and a median return on equity of just 2% over the last 3 years [E28]. Finally, earnings are artificially inflated by other income amounting to Rs 1.13 Cr [E54], undermining the quality of the core business performance.
